effects.log: "Your footwork is still lazy." It takes three months to reach {him}. It takes {him} a year to answer: "I know."

choices.text: Tell the rest of them

effects.log: You mention it, at the morning form, in an unconcerned voice, and then you make them do it again. They have never trained so hard.

events.text: {npc} comes back at last with grey in {his} hair and {gyb_piece} at {his} side and asks, formally, for your correction. You look at the first form. It is very good. It is very good in a way you never taught, and there is one wrong thing in the second step, and it is better than what you had.

choices.text: Correct the wrong thing anyway

effects.log: "Again," you say. {He} does it again. You are both very happy, and neither of you would ever admit to it.

choices.text: Ask {him} to show you that second step

effects.log: You have not asked anyone to show you anything in some time. {He} does not smile. {He} shows you, slowly. It takes the rest of the month, and you are bad at it.

events.text: A young person turns up at your gate asking to be taught. They have been told about you by a teacher who carries your old {gyb_word}. They do not know any of the story. "My master says you are the only one who ever made {him} cry," they say cheerfully. So that is what {npc} is telling people.

choices.text: Take them in

effects.log: You take them on, and you are every bit as bad as the story says. They last. They write to {npc}, you later learn, with complaints. You gather it is a great success.

choices.text: Send them back with a message

effects.log: "Tell {him} I made {him} cry twice." They go. There is a parcel, some months later: a very small wooden sword.

events.text: They bring {gyb_piece} home wrapped in a cloth, with its straps cleaned, because whoever laid out the body knew what they were doing. It is heavier than you remember. There is a nick you do not know. You go through its marks with your thumb, and every one of them is a thing you were not told about.

choices.text: Take it up again

effects.log: You take it up. It is a while before you stop reaching for it with a hand that expects it to be gone.

choices.text: Hang it in the hall, where it can be looked at

effects.log: It goes on the wall with a lamp under it. Nobody in the house walks past without slowing.

choices.text: Send it into the ground with them

effects.log: You open the grave again yourself. It was never yours, in the end. It only took you a long time to finish giving it.

events.text: A stranger arrives at the gate with {gyb_piece} across their back, walking on a bad leg. They were with the one who carried it at the end, and they promised. They will not stay for a meal. They will not take money. "I was told to say it worked," they say. "For the most part." Then they go.

choices.text: Take it up again

effects.log: It worked, for the most part. You oil it and put it on, and you do not sleep that night or the one after.

choices.text: Run after them and ask how it ended

effects.log: They tell you, on the road, in about ten words. You hang it in the hall, and you never ask anyone anything about that year again.

choices.text: Bury it where they fell

effects.log: You walk the whole way there to do it. Nobody at that crossroads knows who it is for, and they keep the place swept anyway.

events.text: Their things come back to you in a very small box, and under the box, because it will not fit, {gyb_piece}. Somebody has kept up the oil. It is in better order than you ever kept it. You find you are angry about that, and you go on being angry for most of the morning, and it helps.

choices.text: Carry it, and keep it the way they did

effects.log: You learn their way of doing the oil. It takes a while. It is a better way.

choices.text: Give it the wall

effects.log: It goes up. You have put up a good many things on that wall, and this is the first you have had to do twice, because your hands were not steady.

events.text: The house has a new custom, and you did not start it: when someone carries a thing of yours to the end, it comes to you at the turn of the year, and the children line up. So there they are in the cold, with {gyb_piece} on a tray. The smallest is trying very hard not to look at it. You know how that is.

choices.text: Take it up, in front of them

effects.log: You take it up, and you tell them the name of who carried it, and you make them say it back.

choices.text: Tell them it goes on the wall, and that one of them may ask for it one day

effects.log: The smallest looks at it for a long moment. You will have to be careful with that one.

events.text: {npc} comes to you in mourning, with {gyb_piece} at {his} side and {his} chin up, plainly expecting to be told to hand it over. It came down to {him} when {his} parent died. You gave it to the parent. You look at it, and at {him}. "Well?" {he} says. There is a good deal of you in that "Well?"

choices.text: Tell {him} it is {his}, and show {him} how the oil goes

effects.log: You spend the afternoon on it. {He} has been doing it wrong. So did the one before {him}, and you never said.

choices.text: Tell {him} what it has done, all of it, so {he} knows what is on it

effects.log: It has been through more hands now, and some of the worst of it you only heard about. {He} listens to all of it, and {his} chin does not come down.

events.text: Nobody asks you. That is the first thing. You find out at a wedding, when {npc} walks in carrying {gyb_piece} as though {he} had always had it, and nobody but you turns to look. It has been some years since you gave it. You had not thought about where it would go on from there.

choices.text: Go over and say something

effects.log: "Your grip is too high," you say. {He} looks at you for some time. "So I was told," {he} says, and it is your own turn of phrase, and you go and sit down.

choices.text: Let it pass, and watch {him} from across the room

effects.log: You watch. Things go on without you. It is the point of the whole business, you remember, and you have another cup.

choices.text: Tell {him} that is the right answer

effects.log: It is the right answer. It is the only one you ever trusted. {He} takes it home, and {he} reads about it, and it turns out that helps.

choices.text: Teach {him} one thing to do with it

effects.log: You teach {him} one plain cut. {He} writes it down. {He} does it exactly as written, for years, and one day that is enough.

events.text: {npc} turns up at your bedside, or what passes for one this year, with {gyb_piece} in both hands. "You need this more than I do." You open your mouth. "I am not asking," {he} says. You have heard that tone before. You taught it. The piece is very clean, and there are new marks on it.

choices.text: Take it back

effects.log: You take it. It is the hardest thing you have done this year, and you have had quite a year. {He} goes away lighter, and you are not sure which of you that hurts.

choices.text: Refuse. A gift is a gift

effects.log: "I gave it," you say. "Carry it." {He} looks at you for a while, then straps it on again, and stays to make the soup, badly. You feel much better, for some reason.

events.text: {npc} is old now. You never planned for that. {He} puts {gyb_piece} on your table and lowers {him}self into a chair by stages. "I cannot lift it the way it ought to be lifted," {he} says. "It should go on being used." You look at {his} hands. You have held them. They have got so thin.

choices.text: Take it back, and tell {him} what you will do with it

effects.log: You tell {him}. {He} nods, and has a nap in your chair, and you do not wake {him}.

choices.text: Tell {him} to keep it by the bed

effects.log: "It does not need lifting," you say. "It only needs to be there." {He} takes it home, and it is there. You see to the oil yourself after that.

choices.text: Take it, and go and be a problem to someone

events.text: {npc} tells you at the door, because {he} would not put it in a letter. Someone got into the house, past the dog, past the lock and past {him}, and {gyb_piece} is gone. Nothing else was touched. {He} has not slept. "I am sorry," {he} says, and you have not heard {him} say that since {he} was small.

choices.text: Track them down yourself, tonight

ok.log: It takes eleven days and a very frightening conversation with a pawnbroker. You put it back in {his} hands yourself, and you tell {him} about the dog.

fail.log: It takes eleven days to find nothing at all. Someone out there has it, and knows what it is, and is in no hurry. You have a name now, at least.

choices.text: Put word out that you will pay

effects.log: It comes back in a sack, with a note that says "Sorry for your trouble". You have never been so insulted, and you hand it over to {npc} with your own hands.

choices.text: Tell {him} it does not matter

effects.log: "It was a thing," you say. "You are not." {He} does not believe you. Neither do you. But it was the right thing to say, and now somebody out there has it.

events.text: A rival of {npc}'s has been seen with something very like {gyb_piece}. It is a matter of a duel-debt, you hear, and a lie, and a signature on a thing {he} should not have signed. {npc} will not discuss it. {He} has taken to wearing something plain, with a good deal of dignity, and nobody at the table is fooled.

choices.text: Go and ask for it back, politely

ok.log: You are extremely polite. You stay for three days. By the end the rival seems to feel it would be easiest for everyone, and you leave with the piece and a recipe.

fail.log: They are polite back. They have a lot of men and a very high wall. You leave with nothing, and they know your name now.

choices.text: Say nothing. It was {his} to lose

effects.log: It was {his} to lose. You told {him} that when you gave it, more or less. It is a very good rule, and you hate it.

It is a matter of a duel-debt, you hear, and a lie, and a signature on a thing {he} should not have signed. {npc} will not discuss it. {He} has taken to wearing something plain, with a good deal of dignity, and nobody at the table is fooled.

choices.text: Go and ask for it back, politely

ok.log: You are extremely polite. You stay for three days. By the end the rival seems to feel it would be easiest for everyone, and you leave with the piece and a recipe.

fail.log: They are polite back. They have a lot of men and a very high wall. You leave with nothing, and they know your name now.

choices.text: Say nothing. It was {his} to lose

effects.log: It was {his} to lose. You told {him} that when you gave it, more or less. It is a very good rule, and you hate it.

events.text: {npc} steps out of the trees onto the road with {gyb_piece} in one hand. You know it from the way the light goes down it. They have taken very good care of it. "I was hoping it would be you," {npc} says. "Everyone I have cut with this has asked me where I got it. You will not need to."

choices.text: Take it back

ok.log: It turns out that nobody knows that blade like the one who wore the grip smooth. You have it out of {his} hand on the second pass. {He} looks at the empty hand, and looks at you, and runs.

fail.log: It is very strange to be cut by it. It is exactly as good as you always said. You come to on the road with your own blood on you, and {npc} has gone, and {he} has left you the scabbard.

choices.text: Walk past. It is only a thing now

effects.log: {npc} calls something after you. You do not catch it. You walk until dark, with your hand on what you have left, and you do not look back.

events.text: There is a wanted notice in the market for {npc}, who has done some ugly things to some people you do not know, with a piece the notice describes in loving detail. Your name is not on it. Your work is. A very small child is reading the notice aloud, slowly, and getting it all right.

choices.text: Go and finish this

ok.log: You find {him} in the hills, with some trouble. {He} is much better than {he} was. It is not enough. You take {gyb_piece} from {him} and clean it for a long time.

fail.log: You find {him} in the hills. {He} is better than {he} was, and better than you hoped. You get away with your life, because {he} does not bother to follow. It was your best work.

choices.text: Pay for the notice to be doubled

effects.log: It goes up on every post from here to the coast. Someone else will have to do it. It is a coward's way, and you are alive to know that.

events.text: You have known for a while that something was wrong in the house. You did not know it would look like this: {npc} in the yard at dusk, with {gyb_piece} drawn, and the servants all sent away. "You taught me the plain cut," {he} says. {He} has been practising. You can see that from here. It is really very good.

choices.text: Draw what you have left

ok.log: What you have left is one tier down, and you never gave {him} the second cut. It ends with {gyb_piece} in your hand and {npc} on the ground, and neither of you says anything. You do not feel you have won.

fail.log: It is very strange to be cut by it, in your own yard. {npc} stands over you and does not finish it. {He} walks out through the gate with what you gave {him}, and you lie there and look at the sky for some time.

choices.text: Tell {him} to keep it, and go

effects.log: "Keep it," you say. "You will need it." You watch {him} work that out. {He} lowers it by a hand's width, and backs out of the gate. It is the last thing you ever give {him}.

events.text: It reaches you through a rival's agent, as a courtesy, or as a threat. {npc} has been going about with {gyb_piece} to meetings you were not told about. It lends weight. "The one who gave it to me," {he} tells them, "would know." You read that line over several times. You used to admire that voice.

choices.text: Go to {him}, and ask for it back

ok.log: You go home. You put your hand out. There is a very long moment, and then it is a very short fight. {He} is still in the house when you are done. You hold on to the thing, and it is much heavier than you remember.

fail.log: You go home and you put your hand out, and {he} uses it. You had forgotten you taught {him} that, too. When you can stand again the house is empty, and it is your name they are using at those meetings.

choices.text: Let {him} have it, and watch who {he} meets

effects.log: It is cold, and it is useful. You learn all their names. It is a poor sort of thing to have got in return for your best work, and you know that.

events.text: The cup was bad, the night before last, and you were lucky. And this morning {npc} has put on {gyb_piece} to come down to breakfast. It is the first time {he} has worn it in the house. {He} pours your tea. {His} hand is perfectly steady, and {he} asks whether you slept.

choices.text: Put down the tea, and stand up

ok.log: It is done before the tea is cold. It is the worst fight you have ever won. You sit back down afterwards, because your legs will not do anything else, and the piece lies on the table between the bowls where you once set it down.

fail.log: It is done before the tea is cold, and it does not go your way. {He} steps over you to reach the door. "Finish your tea," {he} says. You were married to that person for a very long time.

choices.text: Say you slept very well, and drink nothing

effects.log: You both finish breakfast. It is the most dangerous meal of your life. Afterwards {he} goes out, with what you gave {him}, and you have the locks changed.

events.text: {npc} has come to the gate with {gyb_piece} on {his} back and a good many people behind {him}. You gave it to {him} on a better day. {He} has not come to talk, {he} says. {He} only wanted you to see it first. It has been kept very well. You find you are checking the edge from here, out of habit.

choices.text: Go down to the gate alone

ok.log: You go down alone. The people behind {him} stay where they are, which is the only thing that goes right for {him} today. {gyb_piece} comes home to you with a new mark on it, and you know whose.

fail.log: You go down alone. That was a mistake. {He} does not kill you. {He} wanted you to live to think about it, {he} says, and you are carried in with your own gift's work in your side.

choices.text: Bar the gate. Let {him} shout

effects.log: You bar the gate. {He} shouts for some time, and then {he} leaves, and everyone on the road will hear about that. It was still the right thing to do. Probably.

events.text: There are plenty of people who hate you now, and you have had some time to put them in order. You did not expect to find this name so near the top. {npc} sends you a letter in the good hand you taught {him}: "You told me never to draw it on the house. I have thought about what you meant by the house." You read it standing up.

choices.text: Answer in person

ok.log: You answer in person. {He} has become everything you hoped, which is the difficulty. It takes all you have, and at the end you have {gyb_piece}, and no one left to correct.

fail.log: You answer in person. {He} has become everything you hoped, and you are not what you were. You wake up in a bed that is not yours, in a town you do not know. Somebody has paid the bill in advance.

choices.text: Answer on paper, and correct {his} grammar

effects.log: You send it back with the second line marked. It is petty. It is also the only thing you have ever done that made {him} truly furious, and it keeps you warm for a while.
